mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sonorensin increases S. aureus cytoplasmic membrane permeability in an ONPG beta-galactosidase assay.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:Mode of bactericidal action; xml:fig=4:Figure 4; xml:sec=21:Cytoplasmic membrane permeability

mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports membrane permeabilization in S. aureus under assay conditions; it does not define a single molecular pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Propidium iodide flow cytometry shows membrane integrity loss after sonorensin treatment; 70.0% of treated S. aureus cells stained with PI, comparable to nisin at 68.1%.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:Mode of bactericidal action; xml:fig=5:Figure 5; xml:sec=22:Flow cytometry

mechanism_claims.limitations: Flow cytometry supports membrane integrity damage after treatment, not the upstream molecular binding event.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: SEM after 50 ug/mL sonorensin for 4 h shows roughened S. aureus cell surfaces, debris, and lysis relative to untreated cells.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:Mode of bactericidal action; xml:fig=6:Figure 6; xml:sec=23:SEM

mechanism_claims.limitations: Morphology supports cell-envelope damage but remains an endpoint observation.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Sonorensin inhibits S. aureus biofilm attachment/formation and sonorensin-coated LDPE films inhibit visible S. aureus growth/spoilage challenge readouts.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=3:Biofilm inhibition by sonorensin; xml:sec=6:Bioactive polyethylene film; xml:fig=7:Figure 7; xml:fig=8:Figure 8

mechanism_claims.limitations: These are application/phenotype claims and are not promoted to direct molecular mechanism.
